feedback.worked_solution:
From part $2,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{-7}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{15+9\pi }{2},
$$

and from the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{-10}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-10}^{-7}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-7}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information into the above gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-10}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{\pi -15}{2}+\frac{15+9\pi }{2}=5\pi \end{aligned}
$$
